title: Small Business Grants: 2026 Guide To Free Funding
summary: Looking for small business grants in 2026? This guide covers free funding options, eligibility, and how to apply so you can compete and win.
body_markdown:
Small business grants are free money, and billions of dollars worth go unclaimed every year because most owners don't know where to look or assume they won't qualify. We work with more than 100,000 small businesses across the country, and the ones that get funded aren't just lucky. They're organized.


This guide breaks down what's available in 2026, who qualifies, and exactly what you need to do to have a real shot at winning.


## TL;DR: What you need to know about small business grants in 2026


Here's what every small business owner should know before applying.


- Small business grants are free money. Unlike loans, you don't pay them back or give up equity.
- Federal programs like SBIR/STTR fund research and innovation, particularly for science and tech businesses.
- State and local grants vary widely by location. A quick search for "\[your state\] small business grants 2026" is the fastest way to find what's available near you.
- Corporate grants (from programs like the Breva Thrive Grant, Nav Small Business Grant, and NASE Growth Grant) run on quarterly cycles, giving you multiple shots per year.
- Eligibility matters. Most grants have specific requirements around revenue, employee count, industry, or ownership demographics.
- The best applicants are prepared. Clean payroll records, documented labor costs, and organized financial data make a huge difference when reviewers are comparing hundreds of applications.

## What are small business grants and how do they work?


A small business grant is funding you receive from a government agency, corporation, or foundation with no repayment required. Unlike a loan, small business grants don't add debt or cost you equity. You also don't give up equity, which makes grants one of the most valuable forms of business financing available.


Grants are awarded competitively. Reviewers look at your business plan, financial health, community impact, and how well you fit the small business grants program's specific criteria. That last part matters more than most people realize.


Here's what typically happens after you apply:


- Your application is reviewed against eligibility requirements
- Finalists may be asked for additional documentation: payroll records, financial statements, proof of team headcount
- Winners are selected and notified, often within 30 to 90 days
- You receive the funds, either in a lump sum or in installments


The catch? Grants are competitive. Most programs receive far more applications than they can fund. That's why preparation matters: clean records, a clear business story, and documentation ready to go are what separates serious applicants from ones who miss out.


Grant applications can stall when[payroll records](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/payroll-records/) aren't ready to pull. Keeping them organized before you need them is what separates complete applications from ones that stall.


## Types of small business grants available in 2026


Grants come from three main sources: federal agencies, state and local governments, and corporations or private foundations. Each has different eligibility rules, award amounts, and timelines, so knowing which category fits your business is the right place to start.


### Federal small business grants


Federal small business grants are funded through government agencies and tend to be more competitive than corporate programs. The amounts can be significant, though, and for the right business, they're worth pursuing.


SBIR and STTR programs


If you're searching for SBA grants 2026 programs, these are among the most significant you'll find. The Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) programs are the largest sources of federal small business funding in the country. Congress reauthorized both programs through September 30, 2031, with the Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act, signed into law April 13, 2026. Agencies have fully resumed solicitations. Check current opportunities at[the SBIR website](https://www.sbir.gov/) .


Phase I awards typically stay under $150,000, though agencies may issue up to $323,090 without additional SBA approval. These programs are specifically designed for research and development, so they're most relevant to businesses with a science or technology focus. But don't assume you don't qualify just because you're not a tech startup. Agricultural science, environmental research, and healthcare are all active categories.


If you run a home-based business, federal grant eligibility is based on your business structure, revenue, and industry. Whether you operate from a commercial space or a home office doesn't change your eligibility.


USDA Rural Business Development Grants


If your business operates in a rural area, the[USDA Rural Business Development Grant](https://www.rd.usda.gov/programs-services/business-programs/rural-business-development-grant) program may be a fit. These grants support training, technical assistance, and business infrastructure projects for small and emerging businesses in rural communities.


SBA 8(a) Business Development Program


The[SBA 8(a) program](https://www.sba.gov/federal-contracting/contracting-assistance-programs/8a-business-development-program) isn't a direct grant, but it's worth knowing about. Eligible businesses (generally those owned by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals) can access set-aside government contracts, mentorship, and business development training.


### State and local small business grants


Many states run their own programs for restaurants, retail storefronts, and service businesses, from team development grants in Texas to storefront improvement funds in Illinois. Search "\[your state\] small business grants 2026" to find what's currently available in your area.


Your local Small Business Development Center (SBDC) is also a strong resource. They track programs specific to your region and can help you apply. Find[your nearest SBDC](https://www.sba.gov/local-assistance) on the SBA website.


### Corporate and private small business grants


Corporate small business grants have exploded in recent years. Major brands use them to invest in communities, support small business ecosystems, and build goodwill with their customer base. Corporate grants are also among the fastest to disburse: some programs transfer funds within 30 days of award notification, compared to several months for federal and state programs.


Here's what's available in 2026:


### Intuit QuickBooks & Mailchimp Small Business Hero Program


$20,000 cash grants plus approximately $19,300 in QuickBooks and Mailchimp resources, awarded to three winners each quarter, 12 businesses per year total. Anyone can nominate a deserving business, but self-nominations are not accepted. The nominator must not be the owner, an employee, or a family member of the nominated business. Check[the QuickBooks Hero Program page](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/offers/small-business-hero-program/) for the next nomination window. As of fall 2026, the program is between cycles and no new window has been confirmed.


### American Express Shop Small Grants


$20,000 each, in partnership with Main Street America. The 2026 program awarded $10 million or more to more than 500 small businesses. The 2026 application window ran from Small Business Saturday (November 29, 2025) through January 23, 2026. Priority goes to businesses with a brick-and-mortar location in a qualifying main street or commercial district. This program launched as part of America's 250th anniversary. Check[Main Street America](https://mainstreet.org/about/partner-collaborations/amex-shop-small-grant-program) to confirm whether a future cycle is announced.


### Breva Thrive Grant


$5,000 quarterly for U.S. small businesses with demonstrated community impact. The program has a strong preference for businesses directly serving high-need ZIP codes or low-to-moderate income communities. Applications open the first day of each quarter (January, April, July, October) and close the last day of that month. Q4 2026: October 1–31. Apply at[the Breva Thrive Grant page](https://www.breva.ai/thrive-grant) .


### Venmo Small Business Grant


Previously awarded $20,000 to up to 10 businesses per year with fewer than 10 employees and under $50,000 in annual revenue. The program skipped 2025 and has not confirmed a 2026 cycle. Check[the Venmo grants page](https://venmo.com/business/small-business-grant) for current availability before applying.


### NASE Growth Grant


Up to $4,000 per award, with four winners selected each quarter, for members of the National Association for the Self-Employed. Annual members may apply immediately upon joining; monthly members must wait 90 days. Apply at[nase.org](https://www.nase.org/benefits-resources/money-and-taxes/growth-grants) .


### Nav Small Business Grant


$10,000 to the winner and $5,000 to the runner-up, awarded quarterly to any U.S.-based small business. Four chances per year. The application involves posting about your business on social media and a public vote component. Check[nav.com](https://www.nav.com/resource/small-business-grants/) for the current open window.


### Mona Small Business Impact Grant


$5,000 in unrestricted funding for U.S. small businesses with 30 or fewer employees making measurable community impact. Annual program; the 2026 cycle closed March 31. Check[the Mona Impact Grant page](https://www.monaventures.co/impact-grant) for the next cycle.


### FedEx Small Business Grant


FedEx ran one of the most recognized small business grant contests from 2012 through 2024, awarding up to $50,000 annually. The program is now retired. Check[the FedEx small business page](https://www.fedex.com/en-us/small-business/grants.html) in case a new program launches.


### Small business grants for specific groups


Many grant programs target businesses owned by people from historically underserved communities. If you qualify, these can be easier to win. The applicant pool is more defined, and the eligibility match matters a lot to reviewers.


### Women-owned businesses


The[Amber Grant from WomensNet](https://ambergrantsforwomen.com/) awards three $10,000 monthly grants across three categories: the general Amber Grant, a Startup Grant, and a rotating Business Category Grant. One application covers all categories you qualify for. At year-end, one winner from each monthly category pool receives an additional $50,000. Only that year's monthly winners are eligible for the year-end awards. Applications are open on a rolling monthly basis.


The[Cartier Women's Initiative](https://www.cartier.com/en-us/women-initiative.html) offers $30,000 to $100,000 in funding globally, with a focus on impact-driven women entrepreneurs.


The[SoGal Foundation Black Founder Startup Grant](https://sogalfoundation.com/) awards $5,000 to $10,000 to Black women and non-binary founders.


### Veteran-owned businesses


The U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation, with FedEx support, awards grants to five veteran- or military spouse-owned businesses annually with 3 to 20 employees: four receive $10,000 and one receives a $25,000 grand prize. The 2026 program concluded in April; check[hiringourheroes.org](https://www.hiringourheroes.org/small-business-grant/) for the 2027 cycle.


### Minority-owned businesses


Many of these programs also accept LLC owners and sole proprietors. Your business structure rarely disqualifies you, but always read the full eligibility requirements.


## How to find small business grants near you


The best grant for your business depends on where you are, what you do, and who you are as an owner. Here's how to search effectively:


1. Start at[Grants.gov](https://www.grants.gov/) . It's the official database for federal grant opportunities. You can search by business type, industry, and location.
2. Check your SBDC. Small Business Development Centers track local and state programs that don't always appear in national databases. Find yours at[your nearest SBDC](https://www.sba.gov/local-assistance) .
3. Search "\[your city or county\] small business grant 2026". Local economic development offices and chambers of commerce often run smaller programs with less competition.
4. Follow industry associations. If you're in food service, healthcare, retail, or construction, your industry's trade association may have a grant database or funding partnerships.


### How to find home-based business grants


Home-based businesses qualify for nearly all the same grant programs as any other small business. If you're looking for home-based business grants (also searched as home based business grants), the good news is that most state and federal programs don't distinguish between home-based and commercial operations. Eligibility is based on revenue, employee count, and business type. Your physical location doesn't factor in.


A few things to know:


- Register your business in your state, even if you operate from home, to qualify for state programs
- SBA resource partners like SCORE and Small Business Development Centers can help identify home-based-specific opportunities
- Federal grant eligibility is determined by your business structure and industry, not whether you work out of a commercial space


## Who qualifies for small business grants?


Small business grants eligibility varies by program, but most look at a combination of these factors:


- Business size: usually defined by revenue, employee count, or both
- Industry: some grants are sector-specific (agriculture, tech, food service)
- Ownership demographics: many programs prioritize women, veterans, or minority-owned businesses
- Location: some grants are limited to specific states, counties, or regions
- Stage: some programs favor startups; others require an established track record
- Revenue: both minimums (you're an active business) and maximums (you're still small)


Before investing time in an application, read the full eligibility requirements. Grants for small business owners come with a wide range of requirements, and many owners waste hours applying to programs they were never eligible for.


This question comes up a lot in small business communities. In one[r/smallbusiness thread](https://www.reddit.com/r/smallbusiness/comments/1leyk3x/grants_for_small_business/) , an owner of a profitable tabletop gaming store with five employees and $2 million in annual sales asked whether grants were realistic. Neither owner was a minority, and the business didn't fall into a targeted demographic. The community's take:


- For-profit, brick-and-mortar businesses outside the typical grant categories find it difficult to secure grant funding
- Most members pointed toward SBA loans, lines of credit, and tenant improvement negotiations as more practical routes
- Grants aren't impossible for these businesses; corporate programs like the Intuit QuickBooks Hero Program and Nav Small Business Grant are open to all
- The realistic path often involves pursuing both grants and alternative funding simultaneously, rather than waiting on a grant alone


## How to apply for a small business grant successfully


Knowing how to apply for small business grants is only the starting point. It's about being the most prepared applicant in the pool. Here's how to approach it.


### Step 1: Gather your small business grant documents.


Most grant applications require financial documentation. Get ahead of this before you start applying.


Common requirements include:


- Business tax returns (typically 2–3 years)
- Bank statements
- Profit and loss statements
- Balance sheets
- Proof of business registration
- Employee hours and scheduling records (some grants require proof of full- or part-time employment status)
- Labor cost-to-revenue ratio reports (grant reviewers increasingly use these to assess how well you manage labor costs)


If you already use Homebase, labor cost reports and timesheet exports pull directly from your dashboard. No manual calculation required.


Grant reviewers want payroll records and labor cost breakdowns to understand how your business operates. When those documents are ready to export in minutes, your application looks organized from the start.[See how Homebase payroll works →](https://www.joinhomebase.com/payroll/)


### Step 2: Write a clear small business grant application.


Your business case is the heart of your application. It needs to answer three questions:


- What does your business do? Keep it clear and specific; reviewers read hundreds of these.
- What will you do with the money? Be concrete. "Purchase a new POS system to reduce checkout wait times by 40%" is stronger than "improve operations."
- Why should you win? Connect your work to the program's goals, whether that's community impact, innovation, job creation, or serving an underserved market.


Here's what works:


- Tie your ask to a specific outcome with a measurable result
- Use real data: revenue, team size, years in business, community impact
- Be honest about challenges; reviewers appreciate candor over polished spin
- Show alignment with the grant's stated mission


If you manage an hourly team, your business case gets stronger when you show team stability. Grant reviewers view low turnover, consistent scheduling, and documented team growth as signals that your business is ready to put funds to good use. If you have data on employee retention or team tenure, include it.


### Step 3: Submit your grant application early and follow up.


- Submit before the deadline (ideally days before, not hours). Technical issues, missing attachments, and last-minute scrambles disqualify more applications than you'd think.
- Confirm receipt. Most programs send a confirmation. If you don't get one within 24 hours, reach out.
- Follow up if the timeline passes. A polite check-in after the stated award date is acceptable and shows you're engaged.


## Small business grants by industry


Grant funding is available across industries, but some sectors have dedicated programs worth knowing about.


### Restaurant small business grants


Restaurant owners have access to a combination of federal, state, and corporate small business grants specifically designed for the food service industry. What often makes the difference between winning and losing isn't the application itself. It's whether your financial records are ready when the window opens.


Primo Stropoli, owner of[Tetta's Market](https://www.joinhomebase.com/customers/tettas-market-case-study-payroll) in rural New York, inherited a fourth-generation business where financial records were entirely manual: "the equivalent of keeping receipts in an old coffee can," as he puts it. After modernizing with Homebase, payroll that used to take hours of manual data entry now takes five minutes a week, with tax forms auto-populated and ready to share with his accountant. That's exactly the kind of organized, audit-ready financial record that grant reviewers want to see.


Programs to know:


### DoorDash Local Business Relief


Fund $5,000 to $15,000, with eligibility expanded beyond restaurants to include bakeries, flower shops, liquor stores, convenience stores, pet stores, and local grocery stores. Activates on a rolling basis when a declared disaster occurs, so applications aren't always open. Check current status at[Hello Alice](https://www.helloalice.com/small-business-grants-and-funding/doordash) .


### Restaurants Care Resilience Fund


Now in its sixth year, the 2026 cycle awarded $1.41 million to 282 California restaurants and caterers. $5,000 in funding for independent restaurants and commercial caterers with one to five locations and under $3 million in revenue per location. California only. Applications typically open June 1 annually. Check[Restaurants Care](https://restaurantscare.org/resilience) .


Restaurant grant applications ask for payroll records and labor cost data. Having all of it in one place means that when a funding window opens, you're ready to apply, not scrambling.[See Homebase restaurant payroll →](https://www.joinhomebase.com/industry/restaurant-payroll/)


### Retail small business grants


Retail businesses are well-served by several corporate grant programs. The American Express Shop Small Grants program (in partnership with Main Street America) specifically targets brick-and-mortar retail businesses on local commercial corridors. The Intuit QuickBooks Hero Program is also open to retail without industry restrictions.


State and local economic development offices often run storefront improvement or business revitalization grants for retailers in designated commercial corridors. Check your local chamber of commerce or SBDC.


### Salon and beauty small business grants


The beauty industry has a growing ecosystem of grant programs, particularly for women-owned and minority-owned businesses. The Amber Grant (WomensNet), SoGal Foundation, and Cartier Women's Initiative are all relevant here. The Professional Beauty Association also runs educational and business development programs worth following.


### Healthcare and wellness small business grants


Healthcare businesses (from private practices to wellness studios) can access grants through the National Institutes of Health (NIH), the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), and state health departments. The SBIR/STTR programs also have significant health-focused categories.


### Home services and trade small business grants


Plumbers, electricians, HVAC technicians, and other trade businesses can access team development grants at the state level, as well as equipment and tools grants through some local economic development programs.


If your trade business operates from a home office rather than a commercial location, you still qualify for most state team development and equipment grants; eligibility is based on your business registration and operations, not your physical address.


## Common mistakes to avoid when applying for small business grants


Most small business grants rejections come down to a handful of preventable errors.


1. Applying for grants you don't qualify for. Read the eligibility section before you do anything else. This alone will save you hours.
2. Generic applications. Every grant has a specific mission. Tailor your application to reflect their goals, not just yours.
3. Missing documentation. A complete application beats a polished but incomplete one every time.
4. Missing the deadline. Many programs close applications at 5pm, not midnight. Submit early.
5. Ignoring the word limit. If the application says 500 words, write 500 words. Reviewers notice when applicants don't follow instructions.


## Alternatives to small business grants


Small business funding grants are competitive, and free grants for small business owners aren't always the right fit. If you've looked at the grant landscape and don't see one that fits, here are other routes worth exploring:


- SBA Microloan Program: loans up to $50,000 for small businesses and nonprofits, often with lower rates and more flexible terms than traditional bank loans. Learn more about[small business loans](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/small-business-loans/)
- SBA 7(a) Loans: the most common SBA loan program, useful for working capital, equipment, and real estate
- Revenue-based financing: a form of funding where repayment is tied to your monthly revenue, not a fixed schedule. Explore more[financing strategies for small business ownership](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/financing-strategies-for-small-business-ownership/)
- CDFI loans: Community Development Financial Institutions offer financing to businesses that may not qualify for traditional loans, often in underserved communities
- Equipment financing: if your funding need is for a specific purchase, equipment financing may be faster and simpler than a grant application
- Angel investors: early-stage funding in exchange for equity, relevant for businesses with high growth potential


The right path depends on what you need the capital for, how quickly you need it, and whether you're comfortable with repayment terms or equity sharing. Many small businesses pursue small business grants and loans simultaneously; there's no rule against it.


## The bottom line on small business grants


Grant funding is real, it's available, and it's worth pursuing. But it takes preparation. The businesses that win small business grants aren't necessarily the most compelling stories. They're the ones that showed up with clean records, a clear plan, and an application that directly answered what the reviewer was looking for.


When grant reviewers ask for payroll records, labor cost reports, or proof of team headcount, those documents should take minutes to pull together, not an afternoon. ## Small business grants FAQs


Do small business grants have to be paid back?


Small business grants do not have to be paid back. There's no debt and no equity given up. Most grants do come with reporting requirements, though. You'll typically need to document how you used the funds and what outcomes you achieved.


How hard is it to get a small business grant?


Getting small business grants ranges from highly competitive to reasonably accessible depending on the program. Federal grants like SBIR/STTR require detailed technical proposals; corporate grants like the Breva Thrive Grant or Nav Small Business Grant have shorter applications. The best way to improve your odds: apply to multiple programs, submit complete applications, and tailor each one to the program's specific goals.


How long does it take to receive grant money?


It varies widely. Federal grants can take six months to a year from application to disbursement. Corporate grants are often faster; some programs notify winners and disburse funds within 30 to 60 days of the application deadline. Check the timeline for each program before you apply so you can plan accordingly.


Can startups get small business grants?


Startups can get small business grants, but eligibility varies by program. Some require at least a year in business or a track record of revenue; others are specifically designed for early-stage businesses. If you're in a research or innovation space, SBIR/STTR Phase I awards are open to businesses at the proof-of-concept stage.


Are small business grants taxable?


Small business grants are generally considered taxable income by the IRS, meaning you'll owe federal and possibly state taxes on the amount received. Some grants from government programs tied to specific purposes may have different treatment, so talk to your accountant before applying to plan for the impact.


Can I apply for multiple small business grants at the same time?


Applying for multiple small business grants at the same time is allowed and is a smart strategy given how competitive individual programs can be. Just make sure your business meets the eligibility criteria for each one, and tailor each application. Copying and pasting the same answers rarely works since each program has its own priorities.


What are free grants for small businesses?


Free grants for small businesses are funding awards that don't require repayment, interest, or equity. Federal agencies, state governments, corporations, and foundations offer them to support growth, innovation, and underserved communities. The word "free" can be misleading, though: most grants come with conditions on how you use the money and require reporting on outcomes.
